verdict.tagline: Endless clicking hides a grinding wall that stalls over time.
for_you_if: you enjoy incremental games with passive idle progression
you like watching numbers grow over long sessions
not_for_you_if: you mind hitting severe progression walls in the late game
you want to avoid unexpected crashes and memory leaks
you dislike microtransactions speeding up the grind

citations.review_text: Easy if you ave auto clicker, would never buy gems for real money tho

Played it when I was younger; wish they would simply add some DLC instead of having ingame gems;
It also takes WAAAAAAAAY too long to "finish" the game.

I played a lot of clicker games and I really enjoyed most of them, but its first time that I say that this clicker is boring-boring af to be precise.
For the first hours or so its nice, but then you just minimize the game window and your dps is grinding everything for you-your click dmg is absolutely worthless compared to dps. Other than that the main reason this game is so bad is the grind, whoever made achievements in the game is a moron that thinks humans have 200 years lifespan and have nothing else to do than grind NOT for several years, but... DECADES to get some achievements... 
P2W in a clicker game... when I saw this ♥♥♥♥ my jaw literally dropped, not just like 6x autoclickers that do 10x clicks per second, but also premium currency-gems/rubies that speed up whole progress and basically skip hundreds of hours for a begginer... 
Game also gets no updates and is very, very simple and gets boring really quick, it starts good-pupms that dopamine real good but then its just doesnt work since its same stuff all over again-INTENDED to be played for like thousands of hours.

Absolutely not recommended, its a waste of time unless you leave it running on your PC while minimized-even with this setup you wont reach anything cool, only the numbers of hp/dps/click dmg will change

Игра Clicker Heroes - это прекрасный пример жанра idle-игр, затягивающий своей простотой и постоянным прогрессом. Сначала вы просто кликаете по монстрам, чтобы заработать золото, но очень быстро появляются герои, которые наносят урон автоматически. Дальше - больше: уровни, престиж, древние, боги и бесконечный прогресс.

Визуально игра проста, но приятна. Музыкальное сопровождение не надоедает. Самое главное - это оптимизация: игра работает плавно даже на слабых устройствах.

Главный минус - это, конечно, "гринд". Но если вы любите наблюдать за растущими цифрами и чувствовать прогресс даже в фоновом режиме, то Clicker Heroes вам точно понравится. Это отличный вариант для тех, кто хочет расслабиться и немного отвлечься, не требующий постоянного внимания. Рекомендую!

citations.review_text: Easy to play chill game - works in background so gathers money while you're offline which is cool! easy to play for kids and adults who just want to zone out a bit!

Clicker Heroes is an incremental idle game that takes the simple idea of clicking enemies and turns it into a massive progression system. Players defeat monsters, earn gold, upgrade heroes, unlock abilities, and continue pushing through increasingly difficult areas. What starts as a basic clicking game slowly develops into a deep optimisation experience.

The biggest strength of Clicker Heroes is its satisfying progression loop. Watching your damage increase, unlocking new heroes, and reaching higher stages creates a strong sense of growth. Even small upgrades can feel rewarding because they contribute to a much larger goal.

The hero system is one of the game's best features. Each hero provides different bonuses, and choosing when to upgrade, replace, or invest in them adds a layer of strategy. While the game is simple to understand, players who enjoy optimisation can spend a lot of time improving their setup.

The idle mechanics are another major advantage. Players can make progress even when they are not actively playing, making it a great background game. Returning after time away and seeing how much progress has been made is one of the most enjoyable parts of the experience.

The presentation is simple but effective. The colourful fantasy style, large variety of monsters, and humorous hero designs give the game personality without distracting from the main progression system.

However, the biggest weakness is repetition. The core gameplay revolves around defeating enemies, earning gold, and buying upgrades, which can become predictable after many hours. Although the numbers continue growing, the basic actions do not change dramatically.

The game can also become heavily focused on waiting and optimisation. Some players may enjoy planning the most efficient progression paths, while others may feel that the experience becomes too passive.

Replay value is very high for fans of incremental games. With many heroes, upgrades, achievements, and long-term goals, playe…
One of the classics. It's a great clicker game with offline earnings and a rebirth system. My favorite part is idling with progression mode on and reading the hero and upgrade descriptions.
A cute, fun easy to play game. If you have to walk away for a few minute it will continue to collect gold so you can lvl your heroes!

claims.claim: The game suffers from performance degradation and memory leaks after recent engine updates, with memory usage exceeding 4GB during active play.

citations.review_text: Whatever engine update they did absolutely killed performance in this game. Never seen lag until that update. There are known memory leaks that they've done nothing to fix. Sad it came to this.

Suprisingly fun at first. But when progress becomes late game it starts feeling a bit pointless. I did a few transcensions. The main problems with it are that it is a second monitor game, yet it requires quite a bit of paying attention to progress at all. Furthermore, it becomes quite laggy after having some decent progression. The last reason especially is why I dont recommend this game.

Game requires a lot of actively playing to make any progress, and stuff like abilities are poorly worded to the point its literately lying about how the game works, and what strategies are available to you, like its trying to sabotage your progress, and has bugs that are over a decade old that further hinder progress.

Also offline progression is useless, so the only way to progress is to keep the game open, which is bad because...

...the longer the game is open the more memory it uses, using over 4GB of ram when playing an active build.

It's adictive, but then the boredom sets in and the progression is too slow to be entertaining and too fast to not be a hinderance. Overall, it gets really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring around the Level 5k mark and ultimately isn't worth it. 
Fun fact, this isn't an idle game. If you leave it for even 10 minutes your progression hits a standstill. Don't fall for the trap.

I haven't played this game for over a year or 383 days but after 250 hours playing this game and completing 57/111 steam achievements. I killed 7.4 million monsters with 2.4k bosses, the highest zone I completed was zone 978, I found 40 relics and made 4.7k upgrades. I made over 7.000e84 gold which is a very big number. It's been an year since I played this game so I would need to relearn how to play this game and maybe one day get all of the achievements. I don't know if there is a leaderboard for this game.

This game is really popular in the clicker genre, much more so than most other games. My best guess about why is that they have some semblence of story involved that keeps you interested. Every new hero has a short blurb about themselves, some have interactions, and for the first hundred hours or so of gameplay new mechanics are introduced to keep everything interesting. After that though, it becomes a massive slog.

It is common knowledge in the community that there are several, big "slowdown points" in the game where your progress is effectively halted for several tens or hundreds of hours of gameplay as you grind. The first one you will probably experience is after unlocking Frostleaf, where the gap between him and the next hero is several restarts away.

These only get more extreme as time goes on. After each slowdown point, the ideal strategy changes, you start grinding again, and then it starts to settle in how little there is of this game. New hero unlocks get slower, so the actual amount of new content you're experiencing turns from streams to drops. You start noticing the repetitiveness in small areas, like the fact that there are only 10 zones to explore that just repeat, or the fact that a lot of upgrade icons have repeated sprites. There are only 9 abilities in the game, and two of *those* have the same icon. Characters start to get samey or uninspired, and it becomes pretty obvious where content drops began and ended because they feel more "tacked on" than "part of your merry men". Some of the lore starts to make less and less sense. "I thought this guy is a god, why is he several million times less powerful than a power ranger? Or a Centaur with a bow?" With nothing to do but wait for your guys to progress, it all starts to seem silly and pointless. There's only one song in the game, and it gets reptitive. You see one new piece of content every few hours. It starts to dawn on you that this is it, and there is nothing more to experience but big number g…
Great game but be warned, this game's pacing completely falls off a cliff after zone 1 million. I'd suggest stopping there for zone progression.

claims.claim: Several game systems and mechanics, such as specific skills, relics, and mercenary quests, become obsolete or irrelevant as progress continues.

citations.review_text: A game of compromise. Most systems became irrelevant but the dev compromised and kept them, like relic system, like all non-ruby merc quest, like half of the ancients and most outsiders. There are nine skills, and only golden clicks skill remain useful. Still, I wouldn't say it's a bad game, but there are other more interesting idle game out there (I am an achievement hunter so I'll grind for the last few achievements anyway).
